dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: Hi, Nam. You've been in Toronto for a month now. How are you doing?
dialogue.reading: ˈhaɪ, ˈnɑːm. juːv bɪn ɪn təˈrɑːntoʊ fər ə ˈmʌnθ ˈnaʊ. ˈhaʊ ər juː ˈduːɪŋ?

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: I'm OK, thanks. It's exciting, but everything is so different. I think I have a little culture shock.
dialogue.reading: aɪm oʊˈkeɪ, ˈθæŋks. ɪts ɪkˈsaɪtɪŋ, bʌt ˈɛvriθɪŋ ɪz soʊ ˈdɪfərənt. aɪ ˈθɪŋk aɪ ˈhæv ə ˈlɪtəl ˈkʌltʃər ˌʃɑːk.

dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: That's very common. Most exchange students feel the same in their first few months.
dialogue.reading: ðæts ˈvɛri ˈkɑːmən. ˈmoʊst ɪksˈtʃeɪndʒ ˈstuːdənts ˈfiːl ðə ˈseɪm ɪn ðɛr ˈfɜːrst ˈfjuː ˈmʌnθs.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: The cold is the hardest part. It's only October, and I'm already freezing!
dialogue.reading: ðə ˈkoʊld ɪz ðə ˈhɑːrdɪst ˈpɑːrt. ɪts ˈoʊnli ɑːkˈtoʊbər, ənd aɪm ɔːlˈrɛdi ˈfriːzɪŋ!

dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: Ha! Are you used to wearing a jacket and a hat?
dialogue.reading: ˈhɑː! ər juː ˈjuːzd tə ˈwɛrɪŋ ə ˈdʒækɪt ənd ə ˈhæt?

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: Not yet. In Bangkok, I never wear a jacket! But I'm getting used to it.
dialogue.reading: ˈnɑːt ˈjɛt. ɪn ˈbæŋkɑːk, aɪ ˈnɛvər ˈwɛr ə ˈdʒækɪt! bʌt aɪm ˈɡɛtɪŋ ˈjuːzd tu ɪt.

dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: Don't worry, you'll get used to it. What else is difficult?
dialogue.reading: ˈdoʊnt ˈwɜːri, juːl ˈɡɛt ˈjuːzd tu ɪt. ˈwʌt ˈɛls ɪz ˈdɪfɪkəlt?

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: Dinner time. The family I live with eats at six. I'm used to eating at eight!
dialogue.reading: ˈdɪnər ˈtaɪm. ðə ˈfæməli aɪ ˈlɪv wɪð ˈiːts ət ˈsɪks. aɪm ˈjuːzd tu ˈiːtɪŋ ət ˈeɪt!

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: Sometimes, at night, when everything is quiet. I miss my family and Thai food.
dialogue.reading: ˈsʌmtaɪmz, ət ˈnaɪt, wɛn ˈɛvriθɪŋ ɪz ˈkwaɪət. aɪ ˈmɪs maɪ ˈfæməli ənd ˈtaɪ ˈfuːd.

dialogue.speaker: c
dialogue.text: Everyone feels like that sometimes. It takes time to adapt. Call your family often, and try to make new friends here.
dialogue.reading: ˈɛvriwʌn ˈfiːlz ˈlaɪk ðæt ˈsʌmtaɪmz. ɪt ˈteɪks ˈtaɪm tu əˈdæpt. ˈkɔːl jʊr ˈfæməli ˈɔːfən, ənd ˈtraɪ tə ˈmeɪk ˈnuː ˈfrɛndz ˈhɪr.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: Thank you, Ms. Wilson. I already feel better.
dialogue.reading: ˈθæŋk juː, ˈmɪz ˈwɪlsən. aɪ ɔːlˈrɛdi ˈfiːl ˈbɛtər.
